verdict.rationale: Honcho is a memory layer, so contradiction handling is a fair axis. The evidence only shows general background reasoning and that agents can 'build and maintain state' about entities. Nothing documents updating, superseding, or merging stored memories when new information conflicts with old, and the opt-in 'Dreamer working memory' entry is not described as doing so.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on the memory layer to update, supersede, or merge memories when new information contradicts what was stored
